title: Graph visualization in a React application
summary: Render and interact with graph data in a React application. The NVL suite was the initial candidate; after it failed the licence constraint, open-source alternatives were reviewed. Choose a renderer with layouts, interaction handling and React integration.
constraints: Permissive license across the full dependency tree
No install scripts in the dependency tree
No unfixed high or critical advisories
Compatible versions across the chosen graph stack
If npm provenance is unavailable, pin exact versions and record the gap
out_of_scope: Backend graph database and query language
Detailed benchmark against every non-NVL graph library
notes: NVL denied at 2.0.0 and 1.2.2: proprietary licence (Aura or commercial Neo4j only), no repository, no provenance, Node-incompatible packaging, React peer excludes 18.2/18.3. Adopted Cytoscape.js as primary (react-cytoscapejs is stale; use the core API with a ref) and Sigma.js as the large-graph fallback (client-only, WebGL2, pair with graphology and @react-sigma/core). @antv/g6 and @xyflow/react are on hold.
